title: Quantum Mechanics
summary: The quantum mechanics quantum reservoir computing runs on: states, measurement, qubits, time evolution, many-qubit systems, entanglement and mixed states.

children.title: Foundations
children.summary: States are unit vectors, measurements are probabilistic and disturbing, and observables are Hermitian operators.

children.title: Why Quantum Mechanics: The Experiments
children.summary: Three experiments, Stern–Gerlach magnets, three polarisers and a single particle in an interferometer, that no classical picture can explain, worked through with numbers.

children.title: Complex Numbers for Quantum Mechanics
children.summary: Every amplitude in quantum mechanics is a complex number, so this page teaches the handful of facts you need: arithmetic with $i$, the complex plane, modulus and conjugate, Euler's formula, multiplying as turning, and why adding amplitudes produces interference.

children.title: Linear Algebra for Quantum Mechanics
children.summary: Inner products, Hermitian and unitary matrices, eigen-decomposition, matrix exponentials and Kronecker products.

children.title: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
children.summary: Eigenvectors are the directions a matrix only stretches, and eigenvalues are the stretch factors.

children.title: States and Dirac Notation
children.summary: Kets and bras, superposition, bases, and why global phase does not matter while relative phase does.

children.title: Measurement and the Born Rule
children.summary: Probabilities from amplitudes, collapse, measuring in other bases, and the statistics of repeated shots.

children.title: Observables and Uncertainty
children.summary: Expectation values, variance, commutators and the uncertainty relation.

children.title: Commutators and Compatible Observables
children.summary: The commutator $[A, B] = AB - BA$ decides whether two quantities can be measured together, whether the order of measurements matters, how sharp two quantities can be at once, and what stays constant in time.

children.title: Qubits
children.summary: The two-level system: the Bloch sphere, Pauli operators and rotations, gates and circuits.

children.title: The Qubit and the Bloch Sphere
children.summary: Every pure qubit state as a point on a sphere whose coordinates are the expectation values of X, Y and Z.

children.title: Pauli Operators and Rotations
children.summary: The Pauli algebra and rotations exp(−iθP/2), including the rotation that writes an input into a qubit.

children.title: Interference of Amplitudes
children.summary: Quantum probabilities come from adding amplitudes, which can cancel, and this one rule explains the Mach–Zehnder interferometer, why recording which path a particle took destroys the pattern, and how quantum algorithms find answers.

children.title: Gates and Circuits
children.summary: Hadamard and CNOT, an XX coupling from two CNOTs, and Trotter steps for simulating a Hamiltonian.

children.title: Driven Qubits and Rabi Oscillations
children.summary: How a gate is physically made: a qubit in a static field precesses, and a weak oscillating drive at the qubit's own frequency rotates it, giving Rabi oscillations.

children.title: Dynamics
children.summary: Time evolution under a Hamiltonian, the Heisenberg picture and conserved quantities, and the harmonic oscillator.

children.title: The Schrödinger Equation
children.summary: U = exp(−iHt), energy eigenstates, precession of a spin in a field, and Rabi oscillation.

children.title: Schrödinger and Heisenberg Pictures
children.summary: Quantum predictions can be computed by moving the state or by moving the observables; the numbers are identical.

children.title: Wavefunctions, Position and Momentum
children.summary: A particle on a line is described by a wavefunction $\psi(x)$, one amplitude for every position, the continuous version of a qubit's two amplitudes.

children.title: Symmetries and Conservation
children.summary: The Heisenberg picture, why operators that commute with H are conserved, and the parity of the reservoir Hamiltonian.

children.title: The Harmonic Oscillator
children.summary: Ladder operators, Fock states, coherent states and quadratures.

children.title: Many Qubits
children.summary: Tensor products, entanglement and reduced states, mixed states, and spin models.

children.title: Composite Systems and Tensor Products
children.summary: How qubits combine, the basis ordering simulators use, and the exponential growth of the state space.

children.title: Entanglement and Reduced States
children.summary: Bell states, the Schmidt decomposition, the partial trace and entanglement entropy.

children.title: Mixed States
children.summary: The density matrix for a system that is uncertain or only partly seen, and why every reservoir is in a mixed state.

children.title: Spin Models
children.summary: Ising, transverse-field Ising, XX and Heisenberg Hamiltonians, and the disordered all-to-all reservoir model.
